title: MiniWear: Minimizing Flash Wear via Hybrid Persistent Cache for Extended EF-SMR Lifetime
problem: EF-SMR (Embedded-Flash SMR) systems combine NAND flash and Shingled Magnetic Recording disks to balance cost/performance, but flash endurance faces critical degradation due to high traffic-to-capacity ratios causing excessive wear.
motivation: NAND flash lifetime is a key reliability constraint in hybrid storage systems; wear reduction without sacrificing performance is essential for long-term system viability.
method: MiniWear introduces a hybrid persistent cache (PC) composed of Flash-PC and SMR-PC tiers with fine-grained scheduling strategies. At hardware level, the PC is organized as dual tiers; at software level, customized scheduling manages PC resources efficiently. Proactive balancing strategy addresses resource idleness to maximize wear distribution across storage layers.
key_novelty: First hybrid persistent cache architecture for EF-SMR systems with tiered flash/SMR organization and proactive resource balancing to extend flash lifetime.
contributions: Up to 66.67% reduction in flash wear vs. existing methods
Hybrid Flash-PC and SMR-PC tier architecture
Fine-grained software scheduling for PC resource management
Proactive balancing strategy addressing resource idleness
limitations: Evaluation focused on wear reduction; trade-offs with throughput/latency and scalability to larger hybrid systems not detailed.
primary_theme: hybrid persistent cache for flash wear reduction in EF-SMR
